claims.claim: In 2018 the United States generated 292.4 million tons of municipal solid waste, about 4.9 pounds per person per day.

In 2018, almost 94 million tons of MSW were recycled and composted (more than 69 million tons recycled plus about 25 million tons composted), a combined 32.1 percent recycling-and-composting rate; recycling alone was about 23.6 percent.
In 2018 about 50 percent of MSW (more than 146 million tons) was landfilled and 11.8 percent (nearly 35 million tons) was combusted with energy recovery.

Recycling rates differ sharply by material: paper and paperboard was 68.2 percent in 2018, glass about 25 percent, and plastics overall only 8.7 percent; PET bottles and jars were 29.1 percent and HDPE natural bottles 29.3 percent.

EPA describes recycling as a three-step loop: (1) collection and processing, (2) manufacturing recyclables into new products, and (3) purchasing products made from recycled content to close the loop; the chasing-arrows symbol represents this continuous loop.

The EPA waste management hierarchy ranks strategies from most to least environmentally preferred and places source reduction and reuse above recycling and composting, which sit above energy recovery, then treatment and disposal.

Contamination of a recycling bin can spoil an entire load headed to a Material Recovery Facility; problem items such as plastic bags, scrap metal, batteries, and food residue jam or damage equipment and can force material to landfill. 'Wishcycling' is placing non-recyclable items in the bin in the hope they will be recycled.

China's Operation National Sword, phased in from 2017 with a 0.5 percent contamination limit introduced in 2018, restricted imports of scrap plastic and paper and disrupted U.S. recycling, which had shipped much of its scrap to China; a 2022 study found the quantity of plastic landfilled in the U.S. rose 23.2 percent following National Sword.

Downcycling is recycling in which the recovered material is of lower quality and functionality than the original, so many materials are not returned to their original use; recycling markets depend on commodity prices and available end markets for the recovered material.

conflictingEvidence.issue: EPA's overall 2018 plastics recycling rate appears as 9 percent on the National Overview summary and 8.7 percent on the plastics material-specific page.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: Both are EPA figures for 2018; the lesson uses the precise 8.7 percent and notes it as roughly 9 percent.

unsupportedExistingClaims: The generated draft treated 'recycling' as an abstract organizing concept with no factual content about how recycling actually works, its rates, markets, or limits. All of it was discarded.
